speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me. To evaluate your progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger, how long have these symptoms been present, and do you notice any redness, warmth, or a visible lump?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a significant injury. Did you hear a "pop" at the moment of impact, and are you currently unable to bend the finger or make a fist? Also, is there any numbness or tingling in the finger?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Trigger Finger (Stenosing Tenosynovitis) of the right ring finger.

The history of a catch-pull injury combined with the inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint and the finger resting in extension is highly suggestive of a tendon rupture (likely Flexor Digitorum Superficialis) or severe triggering. Can you confirm if there is a visible depression or "gap" at the PIP joint when you attempt to straighten the finger, and do you feel a sudden "snap" when it finally moves? REQUEST IMAGES: Right_hand_XRay_ap.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
